verdicts.reason: A keeps the headline on one line with a clear left/right split (logo, can and circle up top, copy and CTA below), but the can is small and jammed into the top-right circle, and the two-line body copy is very small and sits on the peach circle. B wraps the headline so 'fizz' is left alone on its own line, and that oversized headline overwhelms the shrunken can, which is pushed against the top edge. B's CTA label is tiny inside an oversized button and its body copy is a cramped three-line block, which is weaker hierarchy and typography than A.
